claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic as-cast HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Poor oxygen resistance limits the high-temperature use of HfNbTaTiZr.
Applying a thin ALD alumina coating will significantly improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of as-cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The alumina coating will preserve the alloy's intrinsic mechanical properties.
ALD will produce a continuous, adherent, dense alumina layer on HfNbTaTiZr.
The alumina layer will remain stable at approximately 1000 °C in air.
The dense alumina layer acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier.
Blocking oxygen ingress will reduce internal oxidation of the substrate.
Reduced internal oxidation will prevent oxidation-induced degradation of the microstructure and mechanical performance.
Because the coating is external, it will not alter the beneficial as-cast bulk microstructure.
The as-cast bulk microstructure is responsible for the alloy's useful ductility and strength.
After 100 hours at 1000 °C in air under loading corresponding to strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1, coated samples will have markedly better oxygen resistance than uncoated samples.
The coated alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility within the expected 8–16% range.
The coated alloy will retain high-temperature yield strength within the expected 163–530 MPa range.
The protective effect depends on the coating remaining adherent and intact during high-temperature exposure and mechanical loading.
Excessively thick or nonuniform alumina coatings could introduce thermal stresses or alter surface mechanical properties.
An alumina thickness of 50–100 nm is an optimal range for the proposed coating.
